q: 1. The safe compressive strength of ashlar masonry of granite stone in 1:6 cement mortar may be taken as ...........
explain: Ashlar masonry uses finely dressed stones. Granite is a very hard rock, and in 1:6 cement mortar, it can safely support 160 t/m².

q: 2. The indentation marks made on the top of the brick to provide key for holding the mortar is known as ..........
explain: The frog is the indentation on the top of a brick. It reduces weight and creates a mechanical 'key' for the mortar to bond.

q: 3. Cork flooring is essentially used in ..........
options: buildings such as libraries, theatres and broadcasting stations which are to be noiseless
explain: Cork is highly resilient and sound-absorbent, making it ideal for quiet environments like libraries or recording studios.

q: 4. Timber flooring is preferred in ..........
explain: Timber flooring is preferred for auditoriums and dancing halls because it is resilient, provides good acoustics, and offers a comfortable surface for movement.

q: 5. Glass flooring is generally preferred when ..........
options: light is to be transmitted from upper to lower floor
explain: Glass flooring (using structural glass blocks) is specifically used to allow natural or artificial light to pass through to the floor below.

q: 6. Flooring used in bath rooms and kitchens of posh residential buildings is ..........
explain: Marble flooring is used in high-end (posh) buildings for its superior aesthetic appeal, cleanliness, and durability in wet areas.

q: 7. The oxalic acid is spread and rubbed over the floor which has been ground with machine ..........
options: to make the floor surface look smooth and uniform
to fill up any dents that are left on the floor surface
to make the surface appear glossy
explain: Oxalic acid is used during the final polishing stage of terrazzo or mosaic flooring to react chemically and produce a high-gloss finish.

q: 8. The joints provided in wooden floor are
explain: Tongue and groove joints are standard for flooring because they allow for expansion/contraction while maintaining a flush, interlocking surface.

q: 9. Flooring used in both rooms and kitchens of posh residential building is
explain: Marble flooring is preferred in high-end (posh) residences for its aesthetic appeal and luxury status.

q: 10. Generally a layer in between the base and topping is used in some of the floors. This layer is named as under layer and the floors in which this layer is used are
explain: Terrazzo flooring consists of a decorative top layer and a plain cement concrete 'under layer' for structural support.

q: 11. The narrow strips of wood or bands of plaster laid on the floor to act as guides for bringing whole of the work to a true and even surface are termed as
explain: Screeds are long, straight strips used as gauges to ensure the floor topping is perfectly level and uniform.

q: 12. The stones used in flagstone flooring are rectangular square in shape and have thickness of
explain: Standard flagstones are typically 3cm to 5cm thick to provide sufficient strength without excessive weight.

q: 13. Flag stone floor is recommended to be used at
explain: Because it is natural, durable, and hard-wearing, flagstone is used in a wide variety of high-traffic and outdoor locations.

q: 14. The thickness of terrazzo mix in Terrazzo floors should be approximately
explain: The decorative terrazzo topping layer is generally 6mm to 12mm thick, laid over a concrete base.

q: 15. While grinding the terrazzo floor, final cutting is done by the Carborundum stone of Number
explain: Higher grit numbers indicate finer stones; No. 120 is used for the final polishing stage to achieve a smooth finish.

q: 16. The thickness of Asphalt floor varies from
explain: Asphalt mastic flooring is typically laid in a thickness of 25mm to 40mm for standard wear and tear.

q: 17. If single coat plastering is adopted what is its minimum thickness ..........
explain: For internal brick walls, a 12 mm thick single coat of cement plaster is standard to provide a smooth finish.

q: 18. In single coat plastering the thickness of plastering should not exceed ..........
explain: A single coat of plaster should not exceed 15 mm because excessive thickness can lead to sagging or cracking during drying.

q: 19. A vertical strip of mortar formed on the surface to be plastered before first coat, is known as ..........
explain: Screeds are narrow strips of plaster applied to the wall to act as gauges, ensuring the final plaster surface is uniform and level.

q: 20. In a three coat plastering the first coat is known as ..........
explain: The rendering coat is the base coat applied directly to the masonry; it is roughened to provide a key for the next coat.

q: 21. The roughening of the back ground surface to provide necessary key for plastering is called ..........
explain: Hacking involves creating small indentations on smooth concrete surfaces to allow the plaster to bond mechanically.

q: 22. The process of making the back ground rough, before plastering, is
explain: Hacking involves creating small grooves in a smooth concrete surface to improve plaster adhesion.

q: 23. The dadoring in bath room should be upto ..........
explain: In bathrooms, dado (wall tiling) is usually provided up to 2 meters (200 cm) to protect walls from water splashes.

q: 24. The ceiling height of a buildings is the height ..........
options: of the ceiling above ground level
of the roof above ground level
explain: Ceiling height is defined as the vertical distance measured from the finished floor level to the underside of the ceiling.

q: 25. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joint and the face of the pointing is kept vertical and inside the plane of the wall by means of a suitable tool is called ..........
explain: In recessed pointing, the mortar is pushed back from the masonry face to create a shadow line and a decorative effect.

q: 26. The horizontal upper part of a step on which for is placed in ascending or descending a stairway, is called ..........
explain: The tread is the flat, horizontal surface of a step where one places their foot.

q: 27. In stairs, the flier is ..........
options: a vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread
a straight step having a parallel width of tread
the under surface of a stair
the angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal
explain: A flier is an ordinary rectangular step in a flight that has a uniform width.

q: 28. In stairs, the soffit is ..........
options: a vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread
a straight step having a parallel width of tread
the under surface of a stair
the angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal
explain: The soffit refers to the underside of a flight of stairs or an arch.

q: 29. The pointing which is extensively used in brick work and stone masonry face work, is ..........
explain: Struck pointing (where the upper edge is pressed in) is very common as it sheds water effectively and looks neat.

q: 30. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joints and then finished off flush with the face of the bricks or stones, is called ..........
explain: In tuck pointing, a groove is made in the flush mortar and filled with a narrow strip of white putty to give the illusion of very fine joints.

q: 31. Generally while plastering in ordinary buildings, the ratio of cement and sand used in cement plaster should be ...........
explain: A 1:6 ratio (1 part cement to 6 parts sand) is standard for internal plastering on brick or stone walls.

q: 32. The development of one or more local swelling on the finished plastered surface, is called ...........
explain: Blistering is a defect caused by the presence of unslaked lime or trapped air/moisture behind the plaster coat.

q: 33. In a three coat plastering, the third coat known as ...........
explain: In three-coat work, the coats are: 1. Rendering coat, 2. Floating coat, and 3. Setting (or finishing) coat.

q: 34. In multistoried government buildings, the floor height is usually restricted to ...........
explain: A clear height of 3.4 meters is common in public/government buildings to allow for better ventilation and larger room sizes.

q: 35. In jack arch floor, the rise given to the arch is ...........
explain: Jack arches are very shallow; the rise is typically kept to 1/12th of the span to minimize the vertical profile.
